reason: I already have a cron job calling claude -p and I'd rather add a budget check to it than adopt a pre-alpha tool from one developer. The budget and loop guard are the interesting part, but I can script those myself in an afternoon.
objection: Pre-alpha and a single maintainer: if the loop guard has a bug, it's my team's quota that burns overnight, and I'd be trusting someone else's code more than my own.
would_change_my_mind: A few months of public use with proof the budget and loop limits actually stop runs, plus a way to import my existing scripts as a flow. Then I might self-host the free version.
